text: Police are allowed to lie to your face about the evidence. There is one thing a court has said they cannot do. Put the lie on paper.
provenance: For adults, no state has a law that generally forbids an officer from lying to your face about the evidence.

text: Florida, 1989. Officers manufactured two fake scientific reports, one on a state agency's letterhead, one on a private company's, and showed them to a suspect.
provenance: In State v. Cayward, decided by Florida's Second District Court of Appeal on November 15, 1989, officers manufactured two fake scientific reports — one on the letterhead of the Florida Department of Criminal Law Enforcement, one on the letterhead of a company called Life Codes, Inc.

text: The court upheld the suppression of his confession. Spoken deception, it said, is one thing. Fabricated documents that impersonate a real institution have no place in the criminal justice system.

text: So the line is not the lie. It is the letterhead. They may say it. In some courts, they may not print it.

text: Florida's Supreme Court declined review in 1990 and never ruled on the merits. Which leaves what an officer may say to your face wide open.
